modelBlurb: Rank each of the ten stats within FBS, drop each program’s single best and single worst percentile, average the other eight.

provenance.perception: Weeks in the AP poll and weeks in the AP top 10, every poll since it began in 1936, preseason polls included (data/staging/_staging_ap_poll_success.csv).
provenance.wins: Wins/losses/ties season by season from 1869; a tie is half a win. A few pre-modern programs carry one lump total for the years before ~1936 where game-level records don’t survive — anchored to the NCAA "FBS Records" all-time line where the book publishes one (data/staging/_staging_wins.csv, _staging_wins_ncaa.csv).
provenance.championships: One row per (school, year, selector) from 1901. A year counts only when a recognized selector picked the team — AP, UPI, FWAA, NFF, USA (CFRA/HAF/NCF before 1936); "claim"/"not-claimed" never count. Shared titles count in full (data/staging/_staging_championships.csv).
provenance.allAmericans: Every consensus All-America selection, one row per player, since 1898; unanimous flagged since 1924 (data/staging/_staging_all_americans.csv).
provenance.nflDraft: Every NFL Draft pick by school since 1936, plus the separate AFL drafts of 1960–66; a player taken by both leagues counts once per league (data/staging/_staging_nfl_draft_picks{,_afl}.csv → _staging_nfl_draft_success.csv).

tierDescriptions.Blue Bloods: The programs the data sets clearly apart at the top. Each has been nationally relevant across multiple eras, on sustained excellence rather than one run.
tierDescriptions.Blue Blood Fringe: Just outside the inner circle. Their histories carry too much weight to ignore, and the numbers place them firmly in the tier right below the top.
tierDescriptions.Blue Blood Contenders: The next tier, where the path to the top is less defined. Each has the history and foundation to make a run at blue-blood status, but needs more decades of sustained success — or a truly dominant era — to close the gap.
tierDescriptions.National Powers: Programs the whole country knows, with real title history. The band runs from genuine current risers to powers coasting on an era two or three decades back.
tierDescriptions.National Brands: Recognisable names and real trophy cases, but a clear class break below the powers. Also where newer programs still accruing the cumulative totals land.
tierDescriptions.The Field: Everyone else — mostly regional followings and thin résumés, plus the young programs whose ceilings haven’t been tested by the counting stats.

granular.allAmericans: per-player list for 109/136 programs; the rest (no consensus selections) sit at zero.
granular.conferenceTitles: per-year for 129/136 programs (_staging_conference_titles.csv); the rest use a summary total

dataRange: AP poll 1936–2025; wins season-by-season from 1869; All-Americans from 1898; titles from 1901; drafts from 1936 — our own compilation
